mainTopic: Whether שבט לוי is a קהל, רבי שמעון's five חטאות left to die, and the start of the פרק on the כהן משיח's mistaken ruling
overview: The גמרא first asks whether the כהנים count as a קהל. If they did, they would bring their own bull for a mistaken ruling, and there would be thirteen tribes. רב אחא ברבי יעקב answers that שבט לוי is not a קהל, because only a tribe with land (אחוזה) is called a קהל. To keep twelve tribes, אביי counts אפרים and מנשה as two. רבא objects that they were made equal to the other tribes only for inheritance. The banners and the separate נשיאים do not disprove רבא, since both were arranged for honor. The גמרא then returns to רבי שמעון and brings his ברייתא of five kinds of חטאת left to die, which apply only to an individual and not to the community, as one tradition. The פרק ends, and a new משנה teaches that a כהן משיח brings a פר only when both his ruling and his act were mistakes. The גמרא explains that case with אביי's answer and begins a ברייתא that compares the משיח to the ציבור. That ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If the priests are a congregation, they should bring their own bull
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the earlier claim that the כהנים are called קהל. If so, they should bring a פר for a mistaken ruling, and that would make thirteen tribes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is true, let the priests bring a bull when they sin because of a court ruling! And if you say, yes, they really do, then there are too many tribes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea from just before this, that the כהנים count as a קהל. It shows that this idea leads to a result that cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any group called a קהל that sins because of a mistaken ruling of בית דין brings a פר. If the כהנים are a קהל, they would need their own פר. Saying 'fine, they do' does not work, because then the count of tribes goes above twelve.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, now that you said this (opens a challenge built on what was just said)
A bull brought as a sin-offering, here the communal bull for a mistaken ruling
A legal ruling of בית דין, here a mistaken one
And if you say, yes, that's true (blocking a possible answer)
Too many, more than there should be

phrases.english: But now, if so,
let them bring a bull for a mistaken ruling!
And if you say, yes, that's so,
then there are too many tribes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim made just before this, that the כהנים are called קהל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the כהנים are called קהל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being a קהל means bringing a פר for a mistaken ruling. That would give thirteen tribes, which is impossible.

steps.title: Only a tribe with land is called a congregation
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא ברבי יעקב rejects the earlier approach. He says שבט לוי is not a קהל, because a tribe is called קהל only if it has a portion of land (אחוזה).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אחא ברבי יעקב said: The tribe of לוי is not called a congregation. As it says: 'Behold, I will make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will make you a congregation of peoples...' and goes on to speak of giving the land as a possession. Any tribe that has land is called a congregation, and any tribe without land is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier idea and brings a new approach: שבט לוי, including the כהנים, does not count as a קהל at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins being a 'קהל עמים' to receiving the land as a possession. So a tribe without land is not a קהל. שבט לוי received no portion of land, so it brings no פר of its own, and the problem of thirteen tribes goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: The tribe of לוי (which includes the כהנים)
Is called a congregation
A congregation of peoples (from the פסוק)
A portion of land in ארץ ישראל that belongs to a tribe

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that being a קהל, for the purpose of bringing the communal פר, depends on having a portion of land.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Acha the son of Rabbi Yaakov said:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁבְטוֹ שֶׁל לֵוִי לָא אִיקְּרוּ קָהָל,
phrases.english: The tribe of Levi is not called a congregation,
as it is written: 'Behold, I will make you fruitful and multiply you,'
'and I will make you a congregation of peoples, etc.'
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the פסוק, which promises the land as a possession. That part is the key to the proof.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אֲחוּזָּה – אִיקְּרִי קָהָל,
phrases.english: Any tribe that has a portion of land is called a congregation,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֲחוּזָּה – לָא אִיקְּרִי קָהָל.
phrases.english: and any tribe that has no portion of land is not called a congregation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the idea that the כהנים are a קהל, which step 1 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New approach that replaces the earlier one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהנים, as part of שבט לוי, count as a קהל.
steps.terutzMaskana: שבט לוי has no land, so it is not a קהל and brings no פר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a tribe with an אחוזה is called קהל, so שבט לוי is not a קהל.

steps.title: Without לוי, there are not twelve tribes
steps.stepSummary: If לוי is not counted, the tribes are missing one and fall short of twelve.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the twelve tribes are missing one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אחא ברבי יעקב: if you take לוי out, we only have eleven tribes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the problem was too many tribes. Now, with לוי removed, the problem is too few. The count of twelve has to be kept.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Are missing, are short
The twelve tribes

phrases.english: If so,
the twelve tribes are missing one!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, חָסְרִי לְהוּ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אחא ברבי יעקב's rule from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא ברבי יעקב's rule that שבט לוי is not a קהל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking out לוי leaves eleven tribes, not twelve.

steps.title: אפרים and מנשה count as two tribes
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that אפרים and מנשה are counted as two separate tribes, so the count is back to twelve.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It says, 'אפרים and מנשה shall be to me like ראובן and שמעון.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי fills the missing spot by splitting יוסף into two tribes, אפרים and מנשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as ראובן and שמעון are two full tribes, the פסוק makes אפרים and מנשה two full tribes. So even without לוי there are twelve.

keyTerms.meaning: The two sons of יוסף, each counted as a tribe
Like ראובן and שמעון (full tribes)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
'Ephraim and Menashe shall be to me like Reuven and Shimon.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק that adds a tribe to the count
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without לוי, only eleven tribes remain.
steps.terutzMaskana: אפרים and מנשה are two tribes, so the count is twelve.

steps.title: רבא: they were made equal only for inheritance
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects to אביי. The next פסוק limits the comparison of אפרים and מנשה to the other tribes to inheritance alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: But it is written: 'They shall be called by the name of their brothers in their inheritance.' They were compared to the tribes for inheritance, and not for anything else!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's answer by reading the next פסוק in בראשית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in their inheritance' show that the פסוק makes אפרים and מנשה like ראובן and שמעון only when dividing the land. So אביי's פסוק does not prove that they count as two separate tribes for anything else.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written (introduces a פסוק that challenges something)
Inheritance of land
They were compared, made equal
Another matter

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבא is attacking אביי's answer. He is not giving a new explanation of his own.

phrases.english: Rava said: But isn't it written:
'They shall be called by the name of their brothers in their inheritance,'
for inheritance they were compared to the tribes,
and not for any other matter!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that אפרים and מנשה count as two tribes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק limits their equal status to inheritance, so it cannot make them two קהלים for other laws.

steps.title: But they were separate under the banners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back against רבא: אפרים and מנשה were separate tribes in the camp formation (the דגלים), which has nothing to do with inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: And are they not separate for other matters? But they are separate in the banners!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's limit by pointing to something besides inheritance where אפרים and מנשה counted as two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מדבר, the tribes camped under banners, and אפרים and מנשה each had their own place. That seems to show they count as two tribes even outside of inheritance, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it not so? (a question that signals a challenge)
Separate, divided
The banners under which the tribes camped and traveled in the מדבר

phrases.english: And are they not separate for other things?
But they are separate in the banners!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's limit from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that אפרים and מנשה are equal to the tribes only for inheritance
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: They were separate in the camp formation too, which is a matter other than inheritance.

steps.title: The camps simply followed the land division, to honor the banners
steps.stepSummary: The camp formation was set up to match the land portions, so that each banner would get an equal share of honor. It does not prove that אפרים and מנשה are two tribes for other laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: The way they camped matched the way they inherited, in order to share the honor equally among the banners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. The separation in the banners was just a copy of the inheritance division, done for honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the banners were arranged to match the inheritance, splitting אפרים and מנשה there is part of the inheritance split, not a separate matter. It was done so each banner would have three tribes and equal honor. So the banners do not disprove רבא's claim that the two were made equal to the other tribes only for inheritance.

keyTerms.meaning: As their inheritance, so was their encampment
Encampment, how the tribes camped
To share out honor equally

steps.whatToRemember: שבט לוי is not a קהל because it has no land. אביי counts אפרים and מנשה as two tribes to keep the number at twelve. רבא limits their equal status to inheritance, and the banners do not disprove him, because the camps were arranged to match the inheritance for the sake of honor.

phrases.english: As their inheritance, so was their encampment,
in order to share honor equally among the banners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 and defends רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the evidence is part of the same category (inheritance), not a separate matter
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Splitting them in the banners shows אפרים and מנשה are two tribes for matters beyond inheritance.
steps.terutzMaskana: The banners just followed the inheritance division for the sake of honor, so רבא's limit still holds.

steps.title: But each tribe had its own prince
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer in Step 7. אפרים and מנשה each had their own נשיא, and that has nothing to do with land.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they were separate tribes when it came to the princes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another case where אפרים and מנשה were treated as two separate tribes. Each one had its own נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 explained away the camp formation by saying it simply matched the land portions. Having separate נשיאים seems to have nothing to do with land, so it looks like real proof that they are two tribes for other matters too.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)
Separate, divided
Tribal princes, the leader of each tribe

phrases.english: But they are separate regarding the princes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new proof against the limitation set up in Steps 5 and 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that אפרים and מנשה count as separate only for matters connected to inheritance.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Separate נשיאים is a matter of leadership, not land, so they seem to be two tribes in general.

steps.title: Separate princes were only for honor
steps.stepSummary: Giving each tribe its own נשיא was a way to honor the נשיאים. It does not prove they are two tribes in other laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: That was done to give honor to the princes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the separate נשיאים were only a matter of honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason behind the separate נשיאים was to give each leader his own honor. Since the reason was honor and not tribal status, it cannot be used to prove that אפרים and מנשה are two tribes for other laws.

keyTerms.meaning: That one, that case
To give honor, to show respect

phrases.english: That was to give honor to the princes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the separation (honor), not a statement of tribal status.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Separate נשיאים proves that אפרים and מנשה are two tribes for all matters.
steps.terutzMaskana: The separate נשיאים were for honor alone, so they prove nothing about other laws.

steps.title: Proof from the twelve days of the משכן's dedication
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that משה made twelve days of dedication, instead of seven like שלמה, to honor the נשיאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: שלמה made seven days of dedication for the בית המקדש. Why did משה make twelve days of dedication for the משכן? To give honor to the נשיאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the answer in Step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seven days would have been enough, as שלמה showed. משה stretched the dedication to twelve days so that each נשיא, including the separate נשיאים of אפרים and מנשה, would have his own day. This shows that honor was the reason for the separate treatment.

keyTerms.meaning: Dedication (here, of the משכן or the בית המקדש)
And what did he see, meaning what was his reason

steps.whatToRemember: אפרים and מנשה are treated as two tribes only for land and the things linked to it, and for honoring the נשיאים. That does not make them two tribes for other laws.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
Solomon made seven days of dedication,
so what did Moses see that made him make
twelve days of dedication?
phrases.notes: This was the dedication of the משכן, when each נשיא brought his offering on his own day.

phrases.english: In order to give honor to the princes.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: שְׁלֹמֹה עָשָׂה שִׁבְעָה יְמֵי חֲנוּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 9 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the separate נשיאים were only for honor.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא comparing the seven dedication days of שלמה with the twelve dedication days of משה.

steps.title: So what is the final word on רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The side discussion is over. The גמרא goes back to the main question about רבי שמעון's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What conclusion was reached about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the tribes discussion and asks what the final conclusion is on the main question. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main question was whether רבי שמעון treats a חטאת owned by partners as different from a communal חטאת, as רב יוסף explained, or the same, as אביי explained. The tribes debate did not settle it, so the גמרא now looks for a clear source.

keyTerms.meaning: What came of it? What is the final conclusion?

steps.confusionAlert: 'It' does not mean אפרים and מנשה. It means the earlier question about רבי שמעון and a חטאת owned by partners.

phrases.english: What came of it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the earlier question: does רבי שמעון treat a חטאת owned by partners like a communal one or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion and returns to the main question of the sugya.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי שמעון treats a חטאת owned by partners as different from a communal חטאת or the same.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's five sin-offerings that are left to die
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists five kinds of חטאת that are left to die. It explains why three of them can never happen with a communal offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a ברייתא. רבי שמעון says: five kinds of חטאת are left to die. They are the offspring of a חטאת, the substitute (תמורה) of a חטאת, a חטאת whose owners died, a חטאת whose owners already got atonement with another animal, and a חטאת whose first year has passed. You cannot have the offspring of a communal חטאת, because the community never sets aside a female. You cannot have the substitute of a communal חטאת, because there is no תמורה for communal offerings. You cannot have a communal חטאת whose owners died, because the community never dies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its proof by quoting a ברייתא of רבי שמעון. The ברייתא lists five kinds of חטאת that are left to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For three of the five cases, the ברייתא explains that they simply cannot happen with a communal offering. This begins to split the world into two groups, 'individual' and 'community.' The גמרא will use that split to learn something about partners.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin-offerings that are left to die and are not brought
The offspring of an animal set aside as a חטאת
An animal someone tried to swap in for a חטאת; it becomes holy too
The community, the public

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Shimon says,
five sin-offerings are left to die:
the offspring of a sin-offering, the substitute of a sin-offering,
a sin-offering whose owners died,
a sin-offering whose owners already got atonement,
and a sin-offering whose year has passed.
And you cannot say
the offspring of a sin-offering for the community,
since the community does not set aside a female.
And you cannot say
the substitute of a sin-offering for the community,
since there is no substitute for the community.
And you cannot say
a sin-offering whose owners died, for the community,
since the community does not die.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 11 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's view on whether partners count as a community.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's ברייתא of the five חטאות that are left to die.

steps.title: Learning the unclear cases from the clear ones
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns the last two cases from the first three. All five rules apply only to an individual's חטאת, not to a communal one.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a חטאת whose owners already got atonement, and a חטאת whose year passed, we did not hear a rule for the community. Maybe a communal one would also be left to die? You say: learn the unclear from the clear. The offspring, the substitute, and the חטאת whose owners died are all said about an individual and not about the community. So too, the חטאת whose owners got atonement and the one whose year passed are said about an individual and not about the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by applying the rule of the first three cases to the last two cases as well. The גמרא is building toward its proof about partners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These last two cases could happen with a communal offering, so the text did not settle them on its own. The ברייתא learns them from the three clear cases, which apply only to an individual. The result is that only an individual's חטאת is left to die, and a communal חטאת is not.

keyTerms.meaning: We did not hear, meaning there is no stated rule
Let the unclear case be learned from the clearly stated one
An individual
These things are said, meaning the rule applies

steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא sorts every חטאת into just two groups, individual or community. The גמרא will use this split to decide where רבי שמעון puts a חטאת owned by partners.

phrases.english: One whose owners got atonement, and one whose year has passed –
we have not heard; might they be left to die?
phrases.notes: He means communal offerings in these two cases, which really could happen.

phrases.english: You said: learn the unclear from the clear,
just as we find with the offspring of a sin-offering
and the substitute of a sin-offering and one whose owners died –
these are said about an individual and not about the community,
so too one whose owners got atonement and one whose year passed –
these are said about an individual and not about the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's view on whether partners count as a community.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's rule that all five cases apply to an individual and not to the community, learned by יִלְמוֹד סָתוּם מִן הַמְפוֹרָשׁ.

steps.title: How can you learn the possible from the impossible?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for learning the last two cases from the first three. The first three can never happen with a communal offering, but the last two can.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do we learn something that is possible from something that is impossible?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the method of the ברייתא from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three of the five kinds of חטאת that are left to die could never apply to a communal offering at all. The last two could happen with a communal offering, so the fact that the first three don't apply proves nothing about them. Normally you cannot learn a case that could happen from cases that could not happen.

keyTerms.meaning: we learn (one case from another)
possible (a case that can happen)
impossible (a case that can never happen)

phrases.english: But do we learn the possible
phrases.notes: The "possible" cases are the last two kinds of חטאת. They could happen with a communal offering.

phrases.english: from the impossible?
phrases.notes: These are the first three kinds, which could never happen with a communal offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the learning method used in the ברייתא of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's learning of the last two cases from the first three.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cases that cannot happen with a communal offering cannot teach us about cases that can happen.

steps.title: רבי שמעון received all five rules as one tradition
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learned all five rules together as one single tradition. Where they cannot all apply, none of them apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון learns them in one place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this is not normal learning from one case to another. All five rules were handed down as one package.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון had a tradition that the five rules of חטאת left to die belong together as one unit. Since the first three can never apply to a communal offering, the whole package does not apply there. That includes the last two cases, even though they could happen.

keyTerms.meaning: in one place, as a single unit
learned, received as a tradition

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, all five kinds of חטאת left to die apply only to an individual's offering. They are one tradition, so where some cannot apply, none apply.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon learned them in one place.
phrases.notes: He means he received all five rules as one package, not as separate rules.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the source: it is one tradition, not learning one case from another.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was learning possible cases from impossible ones, which does not work.
steps.terutzMaskana: All five rules are one tradition, so they stand or fall together.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing הורו בית דין
steps.stepSummary: The first פרק of הוריות, called הורו בית דין, ends here.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, הורו בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line said when finishing a פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It closes the first פרק, which dealt with a בית דין that rules by mistake. The next line opens a new פרק with a new משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: we will return to you (said at the end of a פרק)

phrases.english: We will return to you, "Horu Beit Din"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the פרק after the last discussion is resolved.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק of הוריות is complete.

steps.title: When a כהן משיח who rules mistakenly for himself brings a פר
steps.stepSummary: A כהן משיח who rules by mistake and then acts by mistake brings a פר. If either the ruling or the act was on purpose, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a כהן משיח ruled for himself by mistake and acted by mistake, he brings a bull. If he ruled by mistake and acted on purpose, or ruled on purpose and acted by mistake, he is exempt. This is because a כהן משיח's ruling for himself is like a בית דין's ruling for the public.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a משנה about the כהן גדול's mistaken ruling for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He brings a פר only when both the ruling and the act were mistakes. If either one was on purpose, he brings nothing. The reason is that his ruling for himself works like a בית דין's ruling for the public.

keyTerms.meaning: the anointed כהן, the כהן גדול
he ruled (gave a halachic decision)
by mistake, unknowingly
on purpose, knowingly
a bull (brought as a חטאת)
exempt

phrases.english: Mishnah: If the anointed priest ruled for himself
phrases.notes: The "anointed priest" is the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: by mistake, and acted by mistake, he brings a bull.
If he ruled by mistake and acted on purpose,
or ruled on purpose and acted by mistake, he is exempt,
because the ruling of the anointed priest for himself
is like the ruling of the court for the public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק after the closing line of step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן משיח brings a פר only when both his ruling and his act were mistakes. His ruling for himself is like a בית דין's ruling for the public.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to say the first case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first case of the משנה and asks why it was needed, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: "Ruled by mistake and acted by mistake, he brings a bull." That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה had to teach the first case at all. This sets up an answer that will explain the משנה's real point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both the ruling and the act were mistakes, this is clearly the mistaken sin that the Torah says needs a פר. So it seems the משנה is telling us nothing new. The גמרא will now look for a special case that makes the line necessary.

keyTerms.meaning: it is obvious (why say it?)

phrases.english: Gemara: "Ruled by mistake and acted by mistake,
he brings a bull." That is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹגֵג וְעָשָׂה שׁוֹגֵג – מֵבִיא פַּר. פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the first ruling of the משנה in step 17 and questions why it was needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's line that a כהן משיח who ruled and acted by mistake brings a פר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sin done fully by mistake obviously needs a חטאת, so the line seems unnecessary.

steps.title: אביי: he forgot his reason but acted on his ruling
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the first case of the משנה deals with a כהן who ruled, forgot his reason, and acted relying on his ruling. We might have thought this counts as on purpose, so the משנה teaches that he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: What case are we dealing with here? A case where he ruled, then forgot why he ruled that way. When he made his mistake, he said, 'I am acting based on my ruling.' You might have thought: if he had been reminded of his reason, maybe he would have changed his mind. So he should count as acting on purpose and should not be liable. The משנה teaches us that he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from the last step about why the משנה needed to state a case that seems obvious. He explains that the משנה is talking about a special situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new detail is that the כהן forgot the reason behind his ruling but still acted because of it. We might have said his act was not really caused by a mistaken ruling, since he might have changed his mind if he remembered. The משנה teaches that it still counts as a mistaken ruling followed by a mistaken act, so he brings a פר.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Used to narrow a source to a specific situation
A halachic ruling
You might have said. It introduces the mistaken assumption the source is coming to rule out
It teaches us. The source tells us something we would not have known
On purpose, knowingly

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether he is liable. The משנה already says he brings a פר. The question was only why the משנה needed to say it, and אביי shows a case where we might have thought he is exempt.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Here, what are we dealing with?
For example, where he issued a ruling,
and forgot for what reason he had ruled,
and at the time that he erred, he said:
I am acting based on my ruling,
as you might have said:
since if the reason had become known to him,
perhaps he would have retracted,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in square brackets, 'perhaps,' and some don't.

phrases.english: he is like one acting on purpose and should not be liable,
so the משנה teaches us that he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18 about why the first case of the משנה was needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific scenario (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כהן who forgot his reason might have changed his mind, so his act counts as on purpose and he is exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since he acted relying on his ruling, it counts as a mistaken ruling with a mistaken act, and he brings a פר.

steps.title: Source for exempting a deliberate ruling or deliberate act
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case of the משנה: if either the ruling or the act was on purpose, the כהן is exempt. It asks where this rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he ruled on purpose and acted by mistake, and so on, he is exempt. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a person who sins by mistake brings a קרבן based on his own mistaken act. The משנה makes the כהן משיח's קרבן depend on both a mistaken ruling and a mistaken act. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this special rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? A request for the source of a rule
By mistake, unknowingly
And so on. It shows that only the start of a quote is given

phrases.english: The משנה said: If he ruled on purpose and acted by mistake, and so on.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the first case of the משנה to the next case and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the פסוק for the rule that a כהן משיח is exempt unless both the ruling and the act were by mistake.

steps.title: The משיח is like the ציבור
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the words 'לאשמת העם' that the כהן משיח is treated like the ציבור. The ציבור is liable only for a mistaken ruling followed by a mistaken act, so the same is true for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Sages taught in a ברייתא: the פסוק says 'so as to bring guilt upon the people.' This shows that the anointed כהן is treated like the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא that learns the rule from the words of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לאשמת העם' link the כהן משיח to the ציבור. In the first פרק we learned that the ציבור brings a קרבן only when בית דין ruled by mistake and the people acted by mistake. So the משיח is also liable only when both his ruling and his act were mistakes.

keyTerms.meaning: So as to bring guilt upon the people (ויקרא 4:3)
The anointed כהן גדול
The community as a whole

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן משיח is like the ציבור. He brings a פר only when he ruled by mistake and then acted by mistake on that ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: This comparison is the basis for all the special rules of the כהן משיח's פר in this פרק.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
It says: 'So as to bring guilt upon the people,'
this shows that the anointed one is like the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'לאשמת העם' compares the כהן משיח to the ציבור, who are liable only for a mistaken ruling followed by a mistaken act.

steps.title: Couldn't this be learned by logic?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues and asks whether the פסוק is really needed, since the rule might be worked out by logic.
steps.simpleTranslation: For one might have thought the פסוק is not needed: can't this be learned through logical reasoning?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is setting up its next move. It is about to suggest a line of logic that would make the פסוק unnecessary, and the reasoning itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a ברייתא says 'והלא דין הוא', it is questioning whether a פסוק is needed when logic might teach the same thing. The logic has not been given yet. It will come in the following lines, and then the ברייתא will show why the פסוק is still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: For one might have thought
Isn't it a matter of logic? It suggests the rule could be learned by reasoning instead of from a פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: This is still the same ברייתא speaking. It has not stopped. It is testing whether its own source from the פסוק is really needed.

phrases.english: For one might have thought the verse is not needed,
since could this not be derived through logic?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 21 by asking whether its source from the פסוק is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק 'לאשמת העם' to teach that the משיח is like the ציבור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If logic could teach the same rule, the פסוק would be extra. This sets up a logical argument that will be tested next.
